stories.title: 2026-27 NBA trade grades: Thunder acquire Nique Clifford from Kings
stories.summary: We're grading the biggest NBA trades of the season, including the deal that sent Nique Clifford to the Thunder.
stories.detailText: The Oklahoma City Thunder and Sacramento Kings kicked off trade season Sunday, making a deal to send second-year wing Nique Clifford to the injury-ravaged Thunder for two future second-round picks. How does Clifford help replenish the Thunder's depleted depth alongside reigning MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander ? With three months to go until the Feb. 11 NBA trade deadline, expect more deals as the season goes on. I'm grading every trade and breaking down the ramifications for all teams and players involved. To determine each grade, I'm looking at multiple factors, including the on-court impact and ages of involved players, the cost in terms of draft picks and future financial implications, and the context of the team's short- and long-term outlooks. How risky or certain is the move? And how much does it help or hurt the team's chance to win the championship this season or beyond? Let's get into the latest moves: Quick links: Latest buzz | Trade machine Depth charts Nov. 8: Kings trade G Clifford to Thunder Sacramento Kings get: 2028 second-round pick (via Utah), 2030 second-round pick (via Minnesota) Oklahoma City Thunder get: G Nique Clifford Grade for Kings: C- On the night of the 2025 draft, the Kings traded a future top-16-protected pick from the San Antonio Spurs to Oklahoma City for the No. 24 pick, which they used on Clifford. Less than 18 months later, they're sending Clifford back to the Thunder. That would be a strange use of resources on its own -- two second-round picks is a less valuable package than a protected first -- but the Kings' choices look even stranger when considering what happened in the meantime: Clifford was perfectly capable as a rookie before being inexplicably buried on Sacramento's bench to start his sophomore season. Last season, Clifford averaged 8.6 points, 3.8 rebounds and 2.4 assists in 25.1 minutes per game, and he posted the best on/off swing in Sacramento's rotation. But this season, he's down to 1.6 points in 6.3 minutes per contest. To be fair, Clifford is already 24 years old and appears to have a limited NBA ceiling. If the Kings truly concluded that he didn't fit on their roster anymore, then at least they got some draft capital back for him. But it's unclear why they would have come to that conclusion, given his play in 1,932 NBA minutes so far. Grade for Thunder: B The Thunder entered the weekend with 21 future second-round picks, which is far more than they'd ever actually have room to use. So they cashed in two of them for an immediate upgrade on the wing, where injuries have stressed even the Thunder's enviable depth. Clifford might not end up playing any role for Oklahoma City come playoff time, but the team simply needs bodies in the meantime, and Clifford should be useful on both ends in a regular-season capacity. And who knows? Place him in the Thunder's excellent development system and he might blow past any theoretical ceiling while offering inexpensive production for the next few years.

stories.title: Thunder get Nique Clifford in trade with Kings
stories.summary: The Thunder have acquired 2025 first-round pick Nique Clifford in a trade with the Kings.
stories.detailText: The Kings have traded second-year wing Nique Clifford to the Thunder for two second-round picks, Oklahoma City announced Sunday. In return, the Kings will receive a 2028 Utah Jazz second-rounder and a 2030 Minnesota Timberwolves second-rounder out of the Thunder's deep asset cupboard. The Kings initially acquired Clifford in the 2025 draft, trading a top-16-protected 2027 San Antonio Spurs first-round pick to the Thunder to move up to the No. 24 pick and grab Clifford. It was the first move of general manager Scott Perry's tenure. But Clifford never caught on in Sacramento and has recently been buried in coach Doug Christie's rotation despite injuries ahead of him, leading both sides -- the Kings' and Clifford's -- to seek a new home for the 24-year-old. The Thunder are in need on the wing after a rash of early-season injuries. Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace , both starters, are out for several months and perhaps the entire season. Wallace tore the labrum in his left shoulder and Williams fractured his left fibula and dislocated his left ankle in the same late October home game against the LA Clippers . That led the Thunder to go searching for help, landing on Clifford, who is making only $3.2 million this season and $3.4 million next season. The Kings, in return, get a pair of draft assets and clear a roster spot as they search for any type of success in a 1-8 start to the season. The Thunder, despite the injuries, are 8-2.

stories.title: Kings trade wing Nique Clifford to Thunder for two second-round picks
stories.summary: The Thunder are looking for wing depth with Jalen Williams out injured.
stories.detailText: Second-year wing Nique Clifford was not getting much run in Sacramento, he was unimpressive in Summer League, but the real question has been: Is that because Clifford is not really an NBA player, or is it because of the Kings and coach Doug Christie's player development and usage? The Oklahoma City Thunder are betting on the latter, as they have agreed to trade for Clifford from the Kings for two second-round picks (Utah's 2028 and Minnesota's 2030), a story broken by Shams Charania of ESPN . The Thunder are looking for wing depth after potential season-ending injuries to Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace. Clifford, the No. 24 pick in 2025 out of Colorado State, had largely fallen out of the Kings' rotation, and the team worked with him to find a new home, Charania reports. Clifford will make $3.3 million this season and $3.4 million next season, with a team option for nearly $6 million for 2028-29. Clifford, a 6'5" wing, was averaging 6.3 minutes per game for the Kings, averaging 1.6 points per game on 35.3% shooting. Will putting him in the Thunder system and their development program change things for the 24-year-old? The Thunder are betting yes. The Kings have just 13 players on the roster and have two weeks to add a 14th player to meet the league minimum.

stories.title: Week 4 Look Ahead: Luka Dončić continues to dominate, while Kon Knueppel is back on the injury report
stories.summary: Luka and Victor Wembanyama had elite performances in Week 3, while the Bulls welcome back center Nic Claxton.
stories.detailText: After Sunday's games, the 2026-27 NBA season will have completed its first three weeks. While devastating injuries dominated early on, historic performances have taken center stage more recently. San Antonio's Victor Wembanyama had a night rarely seen in NBA history, while Lakers star Luka Dončić is on an extreme heater. Let's look back at some of Week 3's key storylines and look ahead to what's to come in Week 4. Five Week 3 Storylines - Luka Dončić has been on a historic heater: With LeBron James no longer in the picture, the Lakers became Luka's "team" for those interested in that kind of conversation. And it also opened things up for him to do even more offensively, if that were even possible. Well, it was, and Dončić has been on a run rarely seen in NBA history. Through nine games, the Lakers guard is averaging 40.1 points, 7.8 rebounds, 7.7 assists, 1.7 steals and 5.8 three-pointers per game while shooting 49.8 percent from the field and 87.3 percent from the foul line. Sure, Dončić is also averaging 4.9 turnovers per game, but his overall production has minimized the impact on his fantasy value. Not only has he scored at least 40 points in four straight games, but Luka has also tallied at least 35 points, five rebounds and five assists in each of his last seven appearances. At this rate, Dončić is well on his way to being the most valuable player in fantasy basketball...and possibly league MVP as well. - Victor Wembanyama's historic night: Wembanyama's averages aren't on par with Luka's, but he's gotten off to the start that fantasy managers expected, based on his preseason ADP. The Spurs center had a huge night in the team's November 4 win over the Mavericks, tallying 52 points, 24 rebounds, two assists, two steals and eight blocks. Wembanyama joined Bob McAdoo as the only players in league history to finish a game with at least 50 points, 20 rebounds and five blocks since blocked shots became an official stat. Also, he joined Wilt Chamberlain as the only players to record at least 50 points, 20 rebounds and eight blocks. Wilt achieved that feat on five separate occasions in his storied career. With Wembanyama not turning 23 until January, this may not be the last time he records a stat line like the one he dropped on Wednesday. - Kristaps Porziņģis stepping away from basketball: Unfortunately, the Porziņģis situation took another turn last week, as the 7-foot-3 center announced that he was stepping away from basketball. He's been dealing with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) since his time with the Celtics, and managing the illness has been a major challenge. Because of Porziņģis' absence, the Warriors have been withholding payment on his contract, and reports suggest the team hopes to trade him for a player who can help immediately. For his part, Porziņģis said in a statement last week that he's willing to work with the Warriors to reach a solution that satisfies all parties. In his absence, the Warriors have relied more on Charles Bassey , whose contract won't be fully guaranteed until January 10. Undrafted rookie Graham Ike even made two starts early in the season, and Al Horford is providing bench depth. - Yaxel Lendeborg is establishing himself as the early Rookie of the Year favorite: Porziņģis' absence was a factor in Golden State's three-game losing streak to start the season, but they've been on a roll ever since. Saturday's overtime win over the Magic extended the Warriors' win streak to seven, with Stephen Curry going off for 41 points on 13-of-19 shooting. The future Hall of Fame guard's big night isn't a surprise. However, Lendeborg has established himself, in the eyes of many, as the early favorite for Rookie of the Year. During the Warriors' ongoing win streak, he has averaged 22.3 points, 6.7 rebounds, 3.9 assists, 0.9 steals, 1.0 blocks and 2.1 three-pointers per game, shooting 53.0 percent from the field and 79.5 percent from the foul line. While many teams go young and bet on perceived upside in the draft, the Warriors prioritized adding a player who can help win now, with Curry and Draymond Green in the latter stages of their respective careers. Lendeborg does that, and he's also looked like a potential cornerstone in the post-Curry/Green era, whenever that may be. - Kon Knueppel makes his season debut...and aggravates his hamstring strain: Injured just before the start of training camp, Knueppel made his first appearance of the season in the Hornets' November 4 loss to the Nets. Unfortunately, he played just under six minutes before aggravating his strained left hamstring and leaving. Knueppel didn't play in Charlotte's November 6 loss to the Celtics, and the Hornets have not provided a return timeline. Making things worse for the Hornets, Brandon Miller left that game with groin tightness, and neither Moussa Diabaté (quad) nor Dennis Schröder (thigh) played against the Celtics. Naz Reid struggled the last time out, shooting 6-of-17 from the field, and his start in Charlotte has not gone as smoothly as many hoped. But with injuries, the Hornets will need more from Reid. Five Week 4 Storylines - Jalen Duren to miss at least two more weeks: The Pistons have been without their starting center since the second game of the season when he suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain. Duren's status was updated on Sunday, when the Pistons announced he's cleared to start on-court activities and will be re-evaluated in two weeks. The @DetroitPistons today release the following medical update on center Jalen Duren. pic.twitter.com/OlgwWhBvIa — Pistons PR (@Pistons_PR) November 8, 2026 Paul Reed has filled in at center, averaging 12.8 points, 6.2 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 1.5 steals and 1.2 blocks in 29.3 minutes per game. The Pistons don't need Reed to be a prolific scorer, but he has provided solid fantasy value as Duren's replacement. The disappointing part is that John Collins ' production has dropped compared to his 2025-26 numbers with the Clippers. He's averaging 9.4 points and 5.9 rebounds per game and seems to be struggling to fully grasp his role in Detroit. The Pistons play three games next week, two against the Wizards, which could be a "get right" opportunity for Collins. - Thunder reportedly acquire Nique Clifford: Needing depth due to their many injuries, Oklahoma City reportedly acquired Nique Clifford from the Kings for two future second-round picks. After a decent rookie season, Clifford fell out of the Kings' rotation, averaging 6.3 minutes per game this season. The move to Oklahoma City gives him a fresh start, and he's joining a franchise that has developed young players well in the past. As for the Kings, will they look to add another guard? Kevin Porter Jr. 's name has come up before, and he's still a free agent. Whatever the Kings decide, one thing will remain the same: Darius Acuff Jr. will stay the focal point of their ongoing rebuild. - The Wizards ended Week 3 without Anthony Davis and Deandre Ayton: Davis missed the Wizards' final two games of the week with a sprained ankle, while Ayton exited Saturday's loss to the Thunder with a lower left leg injury. Alex Sarr played 28 minutes on Saturday, finishing with 15 points, 14 rebounds and one assist. He didn't record any defensive stats, but the third-year center has a higher ceiling when Davis is out. Bilal Coulibaly started on Saturday and could retain that role, but he went scoreless on 0-of-8 shooting. The Wizards have a surplus of wings, which lends itself to smaller lineups for longer periods if Davis and Ayton can't play on Monday against the Pistons. - The Nets and Timberwolves have light schedules: Brooklyn and Minnesota are the only teams scheduled to play two games in Week 4. However, the Timberwolves have a silver lining: both games are on light days (Thursday and Saturday). With those games against Dallas and Chicago, low-rostered options like Terrence Shannon Jr. and Bones Hyland may be worth a roll of the dice for streaming purposes. The Nets are also active on Saturday, but their first game is on Wednesday, the busiest day of the week. Nolan Traoré , who has been more productive than many expected before the season began, loses some luster in fantasy leagues because of the schedule. The lighter schedule helps Mikel Brown Jr. , who isn't playing both games of back-to-backs because of the back injury that ended his lone college season early. Also, guard Egor Dëmin (leg) will be re-evaluated at the beginning of the week, and the schedule may open the door for him to return to action. - The Mavericks will play on Saturday and Sunday: Dallas is the only team with games on Saturday and Sunday to close out Week 4. That means fantasy managers rostering Kyrie Irving have to anticipate him sitting out one of those games, at Cleveland (Saturday) and at Boston (Sunday). Caleb Martin started the most recent game Irving missed, a November 2 loss to the Kings, and accounted for five points and six rebounds in 21 minutes. Whether he starts or comes off the bench, Naji Marshall is a better streaming option than Martin on nights when Irving doesn't play. Three Questions 1. How many games will Nic Claxton play before he moves into the Bulls' starting lineup? 2. How much longer will the Raptors be without Kawhi Leonard? 3. Will the Celtics stick with a three-man center rotation all season long? stories.title: Is Luka Dončić playing tonight? Injury update on Lakers star vs. Pistons
stories.summary: The Lakers will be without the driving force of their offense against one of the best defenses in the NBA to start their four-game road trip.
stories.detailText: The Los Angeles Lakers are tasked with facing one of the NBA's best defenses in the Detroit Pistons in the first of their four-game road trip on Sunday, Nov. 8. They'll have the added challenge of doing so without the driving force of their offense. Luka Dončić has been ruled out with lower back tightness, the team announced. Dončić was listed as questionable on Saturday, one day after the leading MVP candidate dropped a season-high 53 points at home against the Portland Trail Blazers . It's a blow to the Lakers (8-2), who will be without Dončić's 40.1 points, 7.8 rebounds and 7.7 assists per night in nine games played this season. He's missed one other game with back tightness. Detroit (6-2), meanwhile, has given up an average of 101.8 points per game, fewest in the league. Amid Dončić's historic stretch of seven consecutive 35-plus point games, the last four of which he's scored at least 40, head coach JJ Redick was asked if there was any danger in relying too much on the two-time scoring champion. "Part of planning and team building and playing an 82-game season is that you're constantly assessing and trying to be better," Redick said on Friday. "... Let's say you're running a nine-man rotation or 10-man rotation. It's rare that you have each guy playing great. The goal is for each guy to play great, but that just doesn't happen so you're constantly tending to things. It's just the NBA. " ... We have to rely on Luka because he's our best player, just like every other team relies on their best player. We still have to coach everyone else and coach the team." The Lakers could be choosing to be proactive with getting rest for Dončić, as they travel to Atlanta for the second night of a back-to-back on Monday. Luka Dončić injury history Dončić does have a history of back injuries during his career. Before this season, he was most recently listed with a back injury in March 2025. He was also listed with back-related injuries during the 2019, 2021 and 2024 seasons. Where does Luka Dončić rank among NBA's best? Dončić entered his third season with the Lakers as the unquestioned leader. He was ranked No. 4 on USA TODAY Sports' top 100 player rankings ahead of the 2026-27 season and is currently No. 1 on Lorenzo Reyes' MVP power rankings. stories.title: Charles Bassey’s play is turning heads in Golden State
stories.summary: The Warriors needed a center, and the guy already in the kitchen is cooking up something special.
stories.detailText: SAN FRANCISCO, CA - NOVEMBER 5: Charles Bassey #28 of the Golden State Warriors looks on during the game against the Miami Heat on November 5, 2026 at Chase Center in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Noah Graham/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Every season I activate this trope to try and inspire a wary Dub Nation who wonders why we don’t replace (insert suspect player) with someone else in the league. You’re in the back seat of your mom’s car, those sweet sweet Golden Arches come into view, and you make your pitch: “Mom, can we PLEAAASEEE get McDonald’s?” And without missing a beat, back comes the dreamcrushing sentence masquerading as a better suggestion: “We got McDonald’s at home.” What’s at home is never McDonald’s, but it’s ground beef, sandwich bread, ketchup, mustard, and relish. You eat it and more often than not depending on who your mama is, it hits. Your tastebuds are awash with flavor and gratitude. Maybe mom was right, maybe you do have McDonalds at home. That’s Charles Bassey for the Warriors right now. When Golden State asked for a real center, the front office looked at the cap sheet and injury report, and said, “we got a center at home.” And maybe the Warriors front office is right, maybe we DO have a big man at home! Charles Bassey is ranked#1 in the entire NBA in per-minute impact (min. 50 MP). Elite production off the bench for the Warriors🏆 • +40 Total Plus/Minus in just 83 MIN • +0.482 Plus/Minus Per Minute • +17.35 scaled Per 36 Minutes #1 in entire NBA #DubNation — Charles Bassey Collector (@BasseyCollector) November 7, 2026 I love Charles Bassey man. He is making the right play every time. — WarriorsMuse (@WarriorsMuse) November 6, 2026 And that is quite the development considering the hope of Kristaps Porziņģis dominating as the big man for the Warriors has effectively died as it looks like he’s retiring from Warriors basketball. The team re-signed him this summer even though he’d missed 90 games over the past two seasons with three different teams. Then there’s Al Horford, who is 40 years old and dealing with a body banged up from years of playoff warfare. Horford is a professional basketball genius. But asking him to play 30 minutes a night in November is not gonna have him available for any kinda playoff run in the spring. And of course the Warriors can always counter with the grizzled, undersized legend Draymond Green at center. That works until Draymond does Draymond things and gets ejected two minutes into the third quarter, which brings us to the night the center at home showed up. On Nov. 2 against the Suns, Golden State trailed by 17. Draymond had been thrown out for body slamming one Phoenix player and quasi strangling Dillon Brooks (rightfully so). That’s when Bassey had a career night, scoring 19 points on 7-of-10 shooting, grabbed 8 rebounds and finished +10. After Draymond’s ejection, the Warriors outscored Phoenix 59-45. He also built a connection with rookie Yaxel Lendeborg. Four of Lendeborg’s five assists that night went to Bassey. Every time the rookie lofted the ball near the rim, Bassey caught it and finished. After the game, Bassey called out the Suns for “fake toughness.” The center at home has a little seasoning on him, don’t he? This wasn’t a one-night fluke. The Warriors started 0-3, then won seven straight to get to 7-3, and Bassey was in the middle of it: He has a +34 plus-minus over the seven-game streak, and +33 in the five games where he played real minutes His 15.7 rebounds per 36 minutes ranks second in the NBA He’s shooting 63.6% from the field and 88.2% from the line, with a 25.8 PER. Over the streak he’s averaging roughly 21 points, 15 rebounds and nearly 3 blocks per 36 minutes. Steph will get the headlines tonight and rightfully so. But I have to give massive, massive credit to Charles Bassey for holding the fort and making Steve's gamble of resting Steph for the first couple of possessions of OT look like a genius move. Showing against Franz to help… pic.twitter.com/sZQlVZpQF8 — Joe Viray (@JoeVirayNBA) November 8, 2026 Charles Bassey has been like water in the desert for the Warriors this season. They’ve been looking for a big like that for a while. He’s been awesome. — Esfandiar Baraheni (@JustEsBaraheni) November 8, 2026 Ummm ladies and gentlemen, he’s really balling in his role right now. Here’s the case for more Bassey minutes: in the Orlando game, he played only 11. The Magic won the offensive rebounding battle 24-3 and outscored Golden State 33-2 on second-chance points. The Warriors still won in overtime, because Steph Curry is a supernatural force of nature on the basketball court. Bassey isn’t Porziņģis, a guy who stretches the floor to 28 feet or make anyone’s All-Star ballot. He’s 6-foot-9 and focused completely on rebounding, rim-running and blocked shots. He’s also available to play, and we all know the best ability is availability. Charles mfking Bassey is amazing — Jim Park🏀🌌 (@Sheridanblog) November 8, 2026 Warriors GM Mike Dunleavy may still trade for a center; I absolutely think he should. Using Porziņģis’ contract to match salaries for a real big makes sense, and they have a real chance to pull it off before the trade deadline. Until then, Dub Nation asked for McDonald’s and got told they had a center at home, and so far the one at home is providing a lot of sustenance.

stories.detailText: The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops. The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks . The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics , and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season. Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo 's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season? All season, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from ESPN's NBA insiders. "The business of the NBA comes and plays a part at some point. And I've seen it in my almost 10 years in this league," Tatum said during Celtics media day on Monday . "For me it's more so being grateful for what we accomplished and what he means for this city and to this organization. Just the ups and downs in our career that we were able to grow and learn from and made us the players that we are today. So really just being thankful for those nine years." Suns owner Ishbia says mortgage company woes won't hurt team It's well-known at this point that billionaire Mat Ishbia's mortgage company has had a rough financial stretch. The owner of the Phoenix Suns said Monday that will have "zero" effect on his spending habits when it comes to basketball. In fact, the 46-year-old said he's working on purchasing 14% more of the team, bringing his total to roughly 80%. Ishbia's company -- United Wholesale Mortgage -- suffered a reported $450 million net loss in the second quarter this year, calling into question if the sizable dip would affect his basketball business. The outspoken Ishbia was adamant that nothing would change for the NBA franchise when it comes to spending on players or the fan experience. Williamson not where he wants to be New Orleans Pelicans forward Zion Williamson kept his answer brief when asked how he would summarize his first seven years as an NBA player. "I'm not where I want to be," said Williamson, whom the Pelicans drafted with the No. 1 pick out of Duke in 2019. "I'm not where I need to be." Butler indicates he is 'ahead' in his knee rehab Nearing the eight-month mark since his right ACL surgery , Jimmy Butler III is hesitant to put a specific target date on his eventual NBA return, but he did express optimism in advance of Golden State Warriors training camp. "I promise you I'm coming back, and it's going to be -- I think it's going to be, like, real eye-popping for everybody how I'm still going to be nice," Butler said. "Probably nicer, honestly." Butler has only recently advanced to running, and he will be limited to light on-court individual work when the team begins practice in Hawaii on Tuesday afternoon. It will be several weeks before Butler is expected to advance to a more rigorous stage of his rehab, and the team's lead medical decision-maker, Rick Celebrini, is known for his cautiousness in the later stages of the rehab process. A January or February return can be considered on the optimistic side for Butler, who turned 37 earlier this month. But Butler did say that the strengthening tests on the knee indicate he is ahead of schedule. "My numbers are staggering," Butler said. "They're off the charts. I'm ahead, so they say. So, I just know that all the work that I've been doing, whether it be at home, in L.A., in Europe, in South America, wherever the case may be, I've been doing all the right things. So, I am confident that whenever I come back, I'll be more than ready, I'll be more than healthy and I'll be a better all-around player than I was whenever I went down." -- Anthony Slater Pistons eye "better version" of Cunningham Detroit Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff has held many offseason conversations with All-NBA guard Cade Cunningham about seizing greatness and the necessary steps toward improving after last year's playoff run that stretched to Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals. Bickerstaff has guaranteed "a better version" Cunningham this season, which could be a scary sight after he averaged 23.9 points, 9.9 assists, 5.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 33.9 minutes during 2025-26. But Cunningham also led the East in turnovers per game after finishing with the second most in 2024-25. "I don't have to challenge Cade, and that's why he is who he is," Bickerstaff said. "Because he's pulling. He's not being pushed." Cunningham showed up in a fresh pair of Nike S.T. Charge "Detroit Tough" sneakers in Pistons colors. He will also receive his own signature Nike shoe, which is expected to debut during the second half of the season. "I'm thankful to be in these shoes. I'm thankful to have the opportunity to represent my family in this way," Cunningham said. "Represent where I come from, but then to represent the city of Detroit. "In a city like this, it's a blessing. I'm thankful for it, I don't take it for granted and I'm trying to make the most out of it." -- Eric Woodyard Hornets waive former No. 8 pick Dillingham The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania . Dillingham was traded from the Chicago Bulls on Saturday for Buddy Hield and cash. The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the move. Dillingham, 21, appeared in 30 games for the Bulls last season, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists. SGA on chance at historic third straight MVP At Oklahoma City Thunder media day, guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander discussed the possibility of winning a third straight NBA MVP award and whether that's something he ponders going into this season. "No different than any other year: Try to be the best player I can be, try to implement the things I just worked on," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "The decision for MVP is literally 82 games away. I'm not going to win the award in the first week of the season. ... That kind of recipe for me in the past has kind of worked, and I've been fortunate to win two in a row. "We need to be laser focused on ourselves. We need to take the lessons from that [Western Conference finals] series, for sure, and we did. But it's certainly not something that we overcorrect for, because you end up chasing your shadow, and it prevents you from being your best as you move forward." ESPN's Summer Forecast gave Gilgeous-Alexander the fourth-best chance at the 2027 MVP, behind Victor Wembanyama , Nikola Jokic and Luka Doncic . No player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. -- Baxter Holmes Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title: "It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is." Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures" Simmons "didn't touch a ball for a year" During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season. "The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder." Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers . The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right." Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer. For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren will hold veto power on any trade this season and be an unrestricted free agent next summer. For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent is key. There are eight projected teams that have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract. "I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at media day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do." Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during Pistons media day. -- Bobby Marks Mitchell: LeBron to Cavs made sense "for a lot of reasons" At Cavaliers media day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense." "I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said. After being swept in the Eastern Conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition by acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multiteam trade then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal. Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible with Harden opting out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset. "This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So, what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win. "We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes The departures of three championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander , who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort , Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon. "It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit. "My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood." As fellow OKC guard Jalen Williams added, "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles tendon in Brandon Ingram 's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season. Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year" Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's media day. "I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me." Curry said knee is ready to go for the season Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday in offering positive updates on his injured knee. "Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with." Curry did acknowledge a "management element" but said there are currently no restrictions. Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise Members of the Denver Nuggets ' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer addressed the media on Monday and answered questions regarding Nikola Jokic 's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason. "We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns." LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title. "I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played. "I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it." James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20. No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr. 's contract. "I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that." The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason. Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant Portland Trail Blazers ' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday. "Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player. "I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent." Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant. Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton" Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season. "He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need. "Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks." Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season. Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey . "It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there." Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season. "I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said. Harper addresses role for coming season After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season. "Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in." First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team: "Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language." LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win. "Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything" Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings. "I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors." Haliburton: I am 100% healthy Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season. "I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year." Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team. In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors. Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room. "We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room." "I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control." And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done." Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday. Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft. Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday. Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said. Sept. 26 Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday. 2026 NBA offseason trade grades Sept. 25 What's next for Curry and the Warriors? Stephen Curry 's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings. The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer. By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million. For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer. Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski . The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury. James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July. "[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump." Grizzlies waive Russell The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.title: Luka Dončić sidelined for Lakers-Pistons game due to back tightness
stories.summary: The Lakers announced his status hours before Sunday's 6 p.m. ET tip. He entered Sunday listed as questionable.
stories.detailText: The Los Angeles Lakers have downgraded Luka Dončić to out for Sunday's game against the Detroit Pistons due to lower back tightness. The Lakers announced his status hours before Sunday's scheduled 6 p.m. ET tip in Detroit. He entered Sunday listed as questionable. It's not clear if the injury will sideline Dončić for multiple games. Sunday's game against the Pistons is the first of a back-to-back. The Lakers will visit the Atlanta Hawks on Monday. A six-time All-NBA selection, Dončić is off to a sensational start to the season. Through nine games, Dončić is the NBA's leading scorer with averages of 40.1 points, 7.8 rebounds, 7.7 assists and 1.7 steals per game while shooting 49.8% from the field and 41.9% on 13.8 3-point attempts per game. The Lakers are off to an 8-2 start with Dončić, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler anchoring the lineup in the first season since the departure of LeBron James. Dončić is playing like an MVP candidate as the primary driver behind the Lakers' strong start. The Lakers are certainly hoping that his back injury isn't one that will linger.

stories.summary: Luka Doncic's historically great start to the season has been slowed for Sunday as he was ruled out against the Pistons due to lower back tightness.
stories.detailText: DETROIT -- Luka Doncic was ruled out Sunday because of tightness in his lower back, leaving the Los Angeles Lakers without the NBA's leading scorer against the Detroit Pistons . Doncic has enjoyed a historically great start to the season, averaging 40.1 points, 7.8 rebounds and 7.7 assists per game as Los Angeles is tied for the best record in the Western Conference at 8-2. The Pistons also announced Sunday that All-Star center Jalen Duren , sidelined since last month with a right hamstring strain, will be reevaluated in two weeks. Sunday is the first leg of a four-game road trip for the Lakers, continuing Monday for the second night of a back-to-back against the Atlanta Hawks followed by the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday and Phoenix Suns next Sunday. Doncic has missed one other game to start the season, also because of lower back tightness and in a back-to-back scenario. The Lakers won that game 103-87 against the LA Clippers .

stories.title: Stephen Curry's latest history-making night keeps Warriors rolling
stories.summary: Warriors star Stephen Curry scored 17 of his 41 points in the final seven minutes of a 126-119 overtime win over the Magic, setting another late-career NBA record.
stories.detailText: Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry scored 17 of his 41 points in the final seven minutes of Saturday night's 126-119 overtime win over the Orlando Magic , setting another late-career NBA record at Chase Center. Curry had his second 40-point game in the season's first month, 77th of his 18-year career and -- perhaps most impressively -- 16th 40-point game since his 35th birthday, surpassing LeBron James (15) and Michael Jordan (12) for most all time. "It makes me super proud of the work that's gone in, especially with some injuries and all that," Curry said. "But just the idea I could still get to a certain level, you kind of feed off of that. Especially when it's in a winning fashion like tonight, where we needed all of them. I appreciate the longevity." It's a level of longevity that Warriors coach Steve Kerr called "remarkable." "Work ethic," Kerr said. "Good genes. He's been blessed with a body that's held up. But he's earned that through his strength training, conditioning and fitness level." The Warriors needed every bit of Curry's greatness against a desperate Magic team. Orlando (2-7) flipped a 16-point first-half deficit into a six-point fourth-quarter lead, forcing Curry to make an array of shots down the stretch to force overtime. Curry had 12 points in the final 2:21 of regulation, making two deep 3s, a layup, two free throws and a difficult runner with 25 seconds left to put the Warriors up two. "That was an impossible shot," Kerr said. "So much traffic. That was a 12-foot sort of running float, hook, whatever you call it. To put that off the glass, he's one of one. I don't know if anyone else in the world can make that shot." Jamal Cain tipped in a layup for the Magic with two seconds left to force overtime. Kerr, protecting Curry's minutes at this late stage of his career, put his star on the bench to begin overtime, temporarily cooling him while trusting his team's depth. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg (23 points) and Golden State's reserves continued to deliver early in the season. Backup center Charles Bassey scored the first four points of overtime, and Lendeborg hit a wing 3 to put the Warriors up five. Kerr went back to Curry to close it, stretching him to a season-high 35 minutes. Curry added two floaters and a free throw in overtime to stretch his point total to 41 for the night and deliver the Warriors a seventh straight win, continuing their rise back into the conversation. The Warriors became only the second team (joining the 1950-51 Boston Celtics ) to immediately follow an 0-3 start to the season with a seven-game win streak.

On a night the Brooklyn Nets out-rebounded the Atlanta Hawks by 13, it was their inability to grab rebounds in the final two minutes that lost them the game. Brooklyn wound up losing 124-121 Saturday night, letting a game slip away that was there for the taking. The opponent tonight is in a pretty interesting spot. The Mavericks are looking to get back into the playoffs for the first time in a few years, and they hope the talent on the roster is good enough to get it done. They picked up an NBA Cup tournament victory, 112-100 , against the Utah Jazz at home on Friday night 112-100 NBA Cup win over the Utah Jazz at home Friday night. Game Info WHO : Brooklyn Nets vs. Dallas Mavericks WHEN : 7:30 PM EST (6:30 PM CST) WHERE : American Airlines Center (Dallas, TX) WATCH : YES Network, DAZN, NBA League Pass LISTEN : WFAN radio Nets vs. Mavericks Injury Report Brooklyn Nets OUT – Egor Dëmin (right bone bruise) OUT – Mikel Brown Jr. (back-t0-back) Dallas Mavericks OUT – Tarik Biberovic (right heel bursitis) OUT – Dereck Lively II (right foot surgery) OUT – Sergio de Larrea (right knee sprain) The Game Back-to-backs are tough, and going from Atlanta to Dallas is especially challenging. We’ll see how the Nets do in this one. If they want to win, they’ll need to slow down an old friend. Kyrie Irving is back after missing last year with an ACL tear. He’s averaging 21 points a night while his shooting numbers remain strong, the way he’s getting his buckets looks a little different than what we’re used to. His field goal attempts share of field-goal attempts inside of three feet is at the lowest mark of his career, while his three-point rate is at a career high. Chances are that’ll change the further he gets away from the injury, but it’s certainly something to keep an eye on. Either way, Irving remains a magnetic scorer and a blast to watch when his game is on. Speaking of being on, Nolan Traoré continues to shine. The sophomore guard had 19 points and a career-high five steals in just 22 minutes last night against Atlanta on Saturday. He didn’t play in the fourth quarter, and with Brown Jr. out tonight Sunday, Traoré should get all the minutes he can handle. When Brown Jr. returns, we’ll see if the coaching staff finally starts to give the young guards more playing time alongside each other. The Nets have little to lose by giving that pairing a longer look. Why not give it a shot? We’ll see if the Nets can be great on the glass for all 48 minutes tonight. Brooklyn did great for most of the night, but gave away possessions late with their inability to secure the rebound. Day’ron Sharpe and the team will look to keep Daniel Gafford, Morez Johnson, and the rest of the Mavs off the glass. Speaking of Sharpe, the big guy collected the first triple-double of his career with 12 points, ten rebounds, and a career high 13 assists. Player to watch: Cooper Flagg I try not to fall for hyperbole, but I think I’m gonna make an exception here. Cooper Flagg is so damn good at such a young age and even in his second season as a professional, I think he’s comfortably one of the ten best players in the NBA. He’s so good and at just 19 years old, has a chance to lead the next generation of men’s basketball in the USA in the next decade and beyond. Something that will come with time and experience is the ability to make an impact at the end of games. In a recent game against the San Antonio Spurs, Flagg was relatively uninvolved in the Mavs’ crunch time offense. It was a bit of a surprise considering how excellent Flagg is, and David Trink of Mavs Moneyball has more: “This is not to say that Flagg is incapable. We have seen him take over fourth quarters multiple times this year. If Dallas wants to be a serious playoff contender, however, they can’t have weird nights from him like this. Even if his shots are not going in, he has to demand the ball, and he has to take them. It is his job to take the pressure off Irving late in games. He’s young, so it is entirely possible he was in his own head after a poor shooting game. But learning to be the guy on a nightly basis and flushing the bad performances will be the next step in his evolution.” And that next step is gonna be a doozy. That said, he’s been terrific already and it’ll be exciting to watch him ball out tonight. It’s a homecoming for Julius Randle. The Dallas native is back home and is hoping to put on a show in front of his friends and family. He’s had his good moments so far, but he’s got to cut down on the turnovers. Julius has turned it over at least four times in five out of the last six games and a season high six turnovers last night. The Nets aren’t good enough to withstand that and will need their All-Star to make the most out of possessions every time he has the ball in his hands. stories.title: Jalen Duren will miss at least another 2 weeks due to hamstring injury, Pistons report
stories.summary: Duren has been sidelined since Detroit's October 23 game against Miami.
stories.detailText: The Detroit Pistons provided an update on center Jalen Duren's hamstring injury on Sunday, stating they'll re-evaluate him in another two weeks, though he has been cleared for on-court basketball activity. If Detroit sticks to that timeline, it would be Sunday, Nov. 22, when the Pistons play the Atlanta Hawks in the first game of a quick two-game road trip. Duren initially suffered the injury on Friday, Oct. 23, against the Miami Heat. He picked it up in the second quarter and did not finish the game. He's now missed seven consecutive games with the injury. Without Duren in the lineup, the Pistons are 4-2 and most recently lost 112-106 to the Philadelphia 76ers. If Duren returns in two weeks, he will be back just in time for Detroit to face the Atlanta Hawks on the road on Nov. 22. The Detroit center has played in just two games so far this season, averaging 13 points, 7.5 rebounds and 2 assists per game. The former first-round pick was named an NBA All-Star for the first time in his career last year after managing career highs in points (19.5), helping lead the Pistons to the No. 1 seed in the Eastern Conference before falling to the Cleveland Cavaliers in Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals. Duren was a hot topic over the offseason as he and the Pistons struggled to agree on a long-term contract extension. While trade rumors swirled, Detroit got the deal done, signing him to a five-year, $200 million extension that keeps him under contract through the 2030-2031 season. The Pistons will next face the Los Angeles Lakers at home on Sunday night.

stories.title: Pistons vs Lakers preview: Best Defense vs best offense
stories.summary: Luka Dončić is rolling, but Detroit might have answers.
stories.detailText: Does it get any better than the No. 1 offense versus the No. 1 defense? The Detroit Pistons find themselves in that matchup as the 122-point-per-game Los Angeles Lakers visit Motown tonight. Luka Dončić and the Lakers put up plenty of buckets, but scoring on Detroit is still an impossible task. The Pistons only surrender 101 points a game. Smothering defense every night. Detroit’s defense has its biggest test of the season if Dončić suits up this evening. He’s questionable with lower back tightness. It would be a shame if we’re robbed of Cade Cunningham going head-to-head with another MVP candidate. The bigger shame would be if we miss out on Dončić versus Ausar Thompson. That matchup is like Jerry Rice versus Deion Sanders with how both are operating. GAME VITALS Where: Little Caesars Arena, Detroit, MI When: 6 PM EST Watch: TV20 Detroit/DAZN-DET Odds: Pistons (-4.5) Analysis Detroit hasn’t played since Wednesday’s loss to the Philadelphia 76ers. They’ve had plenty of time to rest up. They’ll need it if Dončić suits up. Dončić is averaging 40 points. He’s shooting 42% on nearly 14 3s a game. He gets to the line more than anybody. It’s basically no stopping Dončić at the moment. This is a Wilt Chamberlain-like hot streak. Those two are the only players to average 40 nine games into the season. Whew, to say he’s balling is an understatement. But tasks like this are why the Pistons employ Ausar Thompson. If *anybody* can slow Dončić down, it’s the best perimeter defender on the planet. Dončić usually has success against quick defenders with wiry strength, but Ausar is bigger and stronger this season. We’ll be keeping tabs on how Ausar takes Dončić’s bumps tonight. Ausar has the quick hands to disrupt things as well. This might be a game where we see Paul Reed getting to the level and blitzing a bunch. J.B. Bickerstaff may decide to get the ball out of Dončić’s hands and force someone else to beat them. Reed is capable of coming to the level on screens and muddying things up. I’m sure Dončić will see some Cade tonight too. Cade won’t make it easy with his sturdy frame. On the other end, the Lakers only have a few perimeter defenders to throw at Cade. Matisse Thybulle is firmly in LA’s rotation as he’s started all 10 games. He’s still a defensive playmaking threat. Cade deals with defenders like this nightly, but Thybulle is a plus defender nonetheless. So is Ziaire Williams. The springy 25-year-old treats every possession as if he’ll never get in the game again if he doesn’t go hard. Those two are solid defensively, and Jake LaRavia competes. Outside of that, Detroit will have plenty of favorable matchups (Walker Kessler is a great rim protector and is off to a good offensive start. He can make a difference). Dončić displays effort and is trying to shake the terrible defender narrative on his name, but attacking him is still the best way to slow him down. Make him work and keep him involved in actions. Austin Reaves falls into the same boat. He’s under Dončić on the Lakers’ best defenders on the team list. Anybody with that matchup should look to be aggressive. Reaves spends most of his time covering shooting guards. Will JJ Redick make Reaves chase Duncan Robinson all night? That’s probably not ideal. Robinson runs even great defenders into the ground. Robinson’s light-em-up stretch continues as he’s fourth in 3s made (35). Only Dončić, Nickeil Alexander-Walker, and Steph Curry have made more. Detroit is letting it fly from deep as a team. According to Cleaning the Glass, 40 percent of their shots are coming from 3 (15th) compared to 31 percent last year (29th). Their rim rate has flipped the other way, but getting Jalen Duren back should rectify that. The best offense versus the best defense is a mandatory viewing appointment. Can Ausar slow down the MVP-favorite? Do the Pistons show why they’re an elite defense and smother Dončić as a team? Does Cade deliver a masterclass against a guy he’ll be compared to for the foreseeable future if he’s in the MVP race? We’ll find out at 6 PM. Be there! Projected starting lineup Detroit Pistons (6-2): Cade Cunningham, Duncan Robinson, Ausar Thompson, John Collins, Paul Reed Los Angeles Lakers (8-2): Luka Dončić, Austin Reaves, Matisse Thybulle, Jake LaRavia, Walker Kessler Question of the day What are your thoughts on Austin Reaves? He reportedly did not want to be drafted by Detroit. Does that still bother you?

Cleveland remains undefeated on that front, while New York keeps stacking dubs on the court. Here’s some of the (very little) latest. Mike Brown on Knicks 109-97 W vs Cavs: "Ugly game but good win…build some positive equity…taking care ball 1st half…important on road…great production bench…Miles, Mo, Andre, Jordan. Our DPOG was Andre Drummond, heckuva performance…Our guys buying into our ability to crash… pic.twitter.com/TBEg7I3HgS — New York Basketball (@NBA_NewYork) November 8, 2026 Mike Brown On giving Landry Shamet more leeway than younger reserves and keeping bench minutes competitive: “Obviously, you looking at a guy like Landry, he may have a little bit more leash than Pac [Dadiet]. Landry’s as close to being a starter as you can imagine for us. Everybody else, they have to play and even the starters and Landry, they do, too.” On Landry Shamet’s standing in the Knicks’ rotation: “About as close to being a starter as you can imagine for us.” On choosing Tyler Kolek over Jose Alvarado as the backup point guard: “But you know, Jose had the first opportunity [against the Nets) and then I gave Tyler an opportunity in the second half and Tyler played well. So I go with Tyler and if I feel I need to make a change, Tyler’s not getting it done in my eyes, I’ll go back to Jose.” On Josh Hart’s ability to contribute without having plays called for him: “Josh is a connector. I don’t think we call a single play for him at any time, he just goes and gets it done. “He rebounds. Our pick and roll defense has been bad, and he’s helped clean it up at times by putting him on the ball. So his versatility defensively is a bonus for us. So he’s definitely going to be missed.” KAT: "It took time to learn how to win at this level…It's much different than college, HS, CYO, AAU…When you finally get to that point of stop trying to prove yourself to everyone, just bring best version of yourself to the court…that's how you prove…whether it's basketball,… pic.twitter.com/zRoOg7hwOW — New York Basketball (@NBA_NewYork) November 8, 2026 Karl-Anthony Towns On facing Cleveland again after defeating the Cavaliers in the Eastern Conference finals: “I mean, they’re a great team. We saw them in the Eastern Conference finals. Obviously, they have another year under their belt with each other, more experience. And we saw what experience does for teams, especially like us.” Tyler Kolek On acknowledging that he underestimated Taylor Swift’s history as a Knicks fan: “Obviously with everything (going on), people have been going back and sending me all the stuff about her going to the games. And she was actually wearing a 13 jersey (in one picture). Probably Joakim Noah back in the day with Carmelo (Anthony). So, I wasn’t up to date on my Taylor Swift Knicks fandom, so that’s on me.” On the reaction to his comments about Taylor Swift and admitting he answered the question poorly: “(The video) was everywhere. Everybody saw it. But it is what it is. For me, it’s just a question that was asked to me that maybe I answered in the wrong way. I take that on the chin. But I love her music. We were just playing it five minutes ago and I’m singing every word to every song. Nothing against her at all.” On being a Taylor Swift fan despite questioning her Knicks fandom: “I love her music. I probably know more songs than anybody else in the locker room. I just misspoke.” "What Mike Brown did last year with this particular team was one of the best coaching jobs I've ever seen" –– MIke Breen pic.twitter.com/MTD26BHVQ7 — New York Basketball (@NBA_NewYork) November 8, 2026 Landry Shamet On returning to Cleveland and remembering the Knicks’ championship run: “It’s human nature, you’re gonna revert back and think back to the last time you were in the building. I had a quick little firing of that walking in for shootaround, but I think the general sense was that was last year. That was great. You can have those memories and hang on to that as long as we want, but ultimately this year is a new year and a new endeavor.” On the benefits of roster continuity and familiarity with Mike Brown: “The biggest thing is just being comfortable with the guys on the floor, second year with [head coach] Mike [Brown]. I think that just breeds confidence. Familiarity breeds confidence. There’s no denying that. It allows you to get to the point of conversations quicker. It makes for a good formula to find success.” On comparing his unpredictable Knicks role to that of a baseball relief pitcher: “Especially with [my] role, I think I take a lot from my buddy Ashby, bullpen guy, you don’t know when you’re gonna get thrown in, what the situation’s gonna be. My job might look a little different from night to night. If I’m changing my approach every night, that’s not setting myself up for a good situation. “I think in the past in my career when I was younger I would try to overcomplicate things and think I have to reinvent the wheel. I try to just keep it as simple as possible, reduce it down to my job, my impact and just play my game.” 👶🏆 https://t.co/oARr089I1A pic.twitter.com/sfndMbGu5z — New York Basketball (@NBA_NewYork) November 8, 2026 Donovan Mitchell On Cleveland’s Saturday loss to the Knicks: “No excuse. These are games that we feel like we should win. We got another tough stretch coming up so there’s no reason to sit here and feel bad and nothing’s won in the first 10 games.” On what went wrong for the Cavaliers: “I think we just gave them too many second-chance opportunities. Then it’s too late, you’re down 20 trying to fight back, but it’s too late.” Peyton Watson On the Cavaliers failing to match the Knicks’ intensity: “Got to bring your A game and we just didn’t do that tonight.” "Rebounding…Rebounding…Rebounding…Rebounding…Rebound…Rebounds…Rebounds…Rebound" –– Kenny Atkinson on the Knicks pic.twitter.com/klwvd52MNi — New York Basketball (@NBA_NewYork) November 8, 2026 Kenny Atkinson On Cleveland continuing to compete despite trailing New York by 18 points: “We could have folded down 18, could have packed it in on a back-to-back, tough week, but we kept at it.” On acknowledging that the Knicks dominated the Cavaliers in the Eastern Conference finals and then won the championship: “They dominated it, and they did it again against San Antonio [in the Finals]. Analytically … there’s an ‘expected score,’ and we’ve won two out of the three games. “I think when you look back on it and take the context of the question, I’m not sure that was taken into account, which I know was a little bit of a lesson for me — like, you can just take a sound bite (and run with it). “I would just say there was no coach more complimentary of the Knicks and honest about our performance and how they dominated us. So you live and learn a little bit with those things. But like I said, 99 percent of my comments were how they dominated us. They were by far the better team. I answered the question, as it was taken, (which was) ‘And you’re down 3-0, what hope do you have of even giving to your guys?’ “We get a lot of information … and I wasn’t lying in that sense, but in no sense was it like, ‘Oh, man, we deserve to be winning.’ Like zero — zero — thought of that.” On why analytics could not outweigh the Knicks’ physical and mental dominance: “We get information that checks our process. All that being said, we were still dominated. It kind of doesn’t matter (what the analytics say) because there is more than that. There is the mental toughness, the physical toughness, the flow to the game, how aggressive you are. There are all these other intangibles that go with that.” On recognizing that the Knicks earned their championship: “They deserved it, and they did it again against San Antonio. Just an incredible, incredible run.” pic.twitter.com/McHRqCt0Bw — Moonball (@moonball30) November 7, 2026

(Photo by Dylan Buell/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Knicks have bobbed over .500 for the first time this season, thanks to yesterday’s return to form against the Cleveland Cavaliers. Over the upcoming week, our heroes will get a second whack at the Ohio Players, plus two beatable opponents. Let’s take a peek at the schedule, shall we? Tuesday, November 10 — Knicks vs. Milwaukee Bucks, 7:30 PM ET (MSG) The Bucks are in a funky funk. Sitting last in the east, they pull into town having lost five straight and seven of their eight games this season. This has not been an auspicious start for new coach Taylor Jenkins. Over the summer, they lost Giannis Antetokounmpo and got younger, which has resulted in struggles at both ends of the floor. Tuesday’s game will be their first meeting with the Knicks this season. The last time they tussled, back on February 27, was a 127-98 New York win in Milwaukee. Our heroes should have many chances to run against Milwaukee and plenty of mismatches to pick on. The Bucks don’t necessarily lack talent—Tyler Herro (acquired in the Giannis trade) leads the team at 22.3 points per game—just hope. Wednesday, November 11 — Knicks vs. Cleveland Cavaliers, 7:00 PM ET (ESPN) The Cavs just got a good look at what New York does well, and boy did it make their eyes water. Four nights after beating the Cavs 109-97 in Cleveland, the two rivals square up again at the Garden. Brunson scored 31 in the first tilt, Karl-Anthony Towns added 29 points and 13 rebounds, and New York led by 19 in the third. Donovan Mitchell found his way to 37, fighting to the end; James Harden died of old age; and Evan Mobley melted into a sweaty puddle under the rim. Cleveland might have been fatigued on Saturday (playing a SEGABABA), and coach Kenny Atkinson will surely try to mix things up in their rematch. We’re curious to see what adjustments are up his sleeve. Jarrett Allen might return from the injured list, so maybe he can keep up with KAT better than Mopey Mobs? Friday, November 13 — Knicks at Indiana Pacers, 7:00 PM ET (Prime Video) The Knicks finish the week in Indiana. The poor Pacers can make a mess of things if you give them the ball and a head start. The 3-7 club has had trouble getting stops and closing games, but you can chalk that up to their leader Tyrese Haliburton being injured again. If he returns for Friday’s game, this could be a different contest. The Pacers can still score in a hurry, especially if you help them with turnovers and lost rebounds. Without Haliburton, Pascal Siakam and Andrew Nembhard have carried the load. Rick Carlisle’s club can turn into layups at the other end, and for as inept as they’ve been at times this season, they can still hit the gas. According to my notes, you’ll watch this one on Prime Video. Knicks in five.

(Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Milwaukee Bucks are looking to halt a five-game slide as they take on Eastern Conference heavyweight Boston Celtics, who beat Milwaukee by seven points without Jayson Tatum on Wednesday. The Bucks and Celtics seem to be moving in entirely different directions. After a slow start to the season, Boston is surging at 7-2 and challenging the Sixers for the No. 1 spot in the conference. Meanwhile, the Bucks are 1-8 and face a daunting schedule that could easily extend their losing streak. On the plus side, Milwaukee’s youth looks strong—Brayden Burries looks great, and Nate Ament is taking exciting developmental steps—and despite the horrible record, we’ve been treated to some really exciting Tyler Herro performances. What else can we look forward to? The Task Ahead The Boston Celtics have been on a tear recently. They’ve won their last two—Wednesday’s back-and-forth win over Milwaukee and a blowout Friday win over the Charlotte Hornets—and have claimed five wins in their last six games. They’re second in the East, half a game behind the Sixers, and, with the addition of Paul George, look like an early title contender. Moreover, aside from some glaring valleys—namely the season opener against the Detroit Pistons—Jayson Tatum has performed at an MVP level so far. His highlights include a 36-point near-triple-double against the Knicks, a 40-point outburst against the Nets (that included a game-winning shot), and a recent 34-point near-triple-double against the Hornets in just 29 minutes. But it hasn’t been all Tatum; Paul George has averaged just under 20 PPG on solid shooting, Derrick White remains the ultimate glue guy, and Neemias Queta anchors one of the league’s best defenses. In three words: Boston is back. In four words: Boston is really back. In five words… you get it. Injury Report Bucks: Bogoljub Markovic: Out (G League assignment) Celtics: Chris Cenac Jr: Out (G League assignment) Player to Watch Derrick White is always fun to watch, especially as he eases into a more offensively significant role in Boston. White is a connective guard with a high basketball IQ and solid playmaking, but he is also an elite defender who can shut down on the perimeter. Against Milwaukee on Wednesday, the veteran guard scored 24 points on 7/18 shooting and added seven assists. White scored 18 points on 6/10 shooting with five assists and four boards in Boston’s demolition of the Hornets. He’ll be a key point-of-attack defender who could frustrate a Milwaukee backcourt prone to turnovers. Watching Brayden Burries go up against one of his draft comparisons in White will also be interesting.
