stories.title: New York Jets vs Kansas City Chiefs: Jets fold in second half, Chiefs cruise to easy win
stories.summary: Another week, another humiliation for Aaron Glenn and the Jets
stories.detailText: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - NOVEMBER 8: Kenneth Walker III #9 of the Kansas City Chiefs celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the second quarter of the NFL football game against the New York Jets at Arrowhead Stadium on November 8, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the New York Jets’ ninth game of the 2026 season, on a gorgeous, warm and sunny day in Kansas City, Missouri, the Jets lost to the Kansas City Chiefs, 35 – 12. The game opened with the Jets on offense. They put together a nice drive, mixing runs and short passes effectively. Breece Hall and Braelon Allen combined to do much of the heavy lifting. The Jets got the ball down to the Chiefs five yard line before they were forced to settle for a chip shot field goal and an early 3 – 0 lead. The Jets defense then stepped up. They recovered a Justin Fields fumble on a quarterback sneak and the Jets quickly had the ball back in Chiefs territory. Unfortunately the Jets did not fully take advantage of the golden opportunity. They failed to get a first down and had to settle for another field goal. The Jets were up 6 – 0 late in the first quarter, but it felt like the points left on the field as they settled for field goals rather than touchdowns would come back to bite them later. The first quarter ended with the Chiefs knocking on the door, looking to go ahead with a first and goal at the Jets 7 yard line. On the first play of the second quarter Mahomes found Kenneth Walker for a touchdown and, despite all the good things that happened for the Jets early, the Chiefs had the lead at 7 – 6. The Jets fought back. They drove the ball near the Chiefs 20 yard before three consecutive plays went backwards. The Jets settled for a 49 yard field goal to regain the lead. Midway through the second quarter the Jets had scored on all three drives to this point, yet had only nine points and a two point lead to show for it. If they didn’t start converting scoring opportunities into touchdowns it was likely going to be another long day for the Jets. It didn’t take long for the Chiefs to take the lead back. Braelon Allen failed to protect the ball with two hands and fumbled. The Chiefs recovered deep in Jets territory. A couple of plays later Patrick Mahomes hit Kenneth Walker for his second touchdown of the game. The Chiefs had a 14 – 9 lead with a little more than five minutes left in the first half. The Jets answered with yet another scoring drive. Again they were forced to settle for a field goal. With a little more than two minutes left in the first half the Jets had scored on four of five drives yet still trailed, 14 – 12. A few plays later the Jets got a strip sack of Mahomes and recovered the ball deep in Chiefs territory. The Jets were unable to take advantage of the opportunity as their drive went nowhere and Jason Sanders missed a long field goal attempt. The Chiefs returned the favor as time ran out, missing a field goal to end the half. The Jets went into the locker room trailing the Chiefs 14 – 12. They had left a lot of points on the field. They had dominated time of possession, scored four times, outgained the Chiefs, out-sacked the Chiefs, led the turnover battle, and still trailed. It would be a surprise if that didn’t cost them the game in the end. The Jets opened the third quarter on defense. It did not go well. The kickoff went out of bounds, giving the Chiefs great field position at the 40 yard line. From there the Chiefs went on a drive ending in a short touchdown pass from Mahomes to Travis Kelce. The extra point gave the Chiefs a 21 – 12 lead. The Jets offense responded with a three and out. Midway through the third quarter the Jets were in serious trouble. Towards the end of the third quarter the Chiefs put together a drive ending in a Kenneth Walker touchdown run. Walker was single handedly dismantling the Jets. The extra point made the score 28 – 12 in favor of the Chiefs as the third quarter ended. The game was all but over. On the Jets’ next drive they moved the ball quickly downfield before Geno Smith was sacked on fourth down, ending the drive. The Jets trailed by 16 points with a little over 11 minutes left. Turn out the lights, the party was over. All those points left on the field in the first half had come back to bite the Jets in the second half. Late in the fourth quarter the Chiefs tacked on another touchdown. They had now outscored the Jets 21 – 0 in the second half as they cruised to an easy victory. Final score: Chiefs 35, Jets 12. The loss brought the Jets’ record to 2-7. A 16th straight season without the playoffs is all but certain. Another November and December talking about next year and the draft looms. What fun awaits as the holiday season approaches! The Jets limp home to take on the first place Buffalo Bills next week. That should be a blast.

stories.title: Chiefs crush Jets 35-12 to end two-game losing streak
stories.summary: Kenneth Walker scored three touchdowns as the Chiefs moved to 6-2 on the season.
stories.detailText: Kenneth Walker had a big hand in the Chiefs' five-game winning streak to open the season and he had a big hand in ending their two-game losing streak on Sunday. Walker caught a pair of touchdown passes from Patrick Mahomes in the first half of the game and he ran for another score in the second half of Kansas City's 35-12 home win over the Jets. The victory moves the Chiefs to 6-2 on the season and Walker is now tied with Jahmyr Gibbs for the league lead with 11 total touchdowns on the season. It's the fifth multi-touchdown game of Walker's first season with the Chiefs and the Chiefs have won all of those games. He did not score in either of their losses, so his importance to the offense probably can't be overstated. Walker ran 18 times for 102 yards and his four catches picked up 41 yards, which gave him more yards from scrimmage on Sunday than he managed in either of the Chiefs' two losses. The Chiefs got a scare just before halftime when Patrick Mahomes hurt his right elbow on a sack by Jets first-rounder David Bailey. The Chiefs lost a fumble on the play, but Mahomes was able to remain in the game and no negative impact on his game was visible over the second half. Mahomes finished 23-of-31 for 242 yards and four of those completions went to Travis Kelce for 72 yards. Kelce also had a one-yard rushing touchdown. Mahomes and Kelce have been joined on the top line of Chiefs stars by defensive tackle Chris Jones for many years and Jones chipped in a pair of sacks of Jets quarterback Geno Smith during the win. George Karlaftis had a pair of them as well and the Chiefs will try to keep things firing on all cylinders in Atlanta next Sunday. One change they could make is with kicker Harrison Butker. He missed another field goal and Justin Tucker is on the practice squad, so the team could opt for a new kicker against the Falcons. Smith was sacked five times . The Jets actually controlled much of the first half and had chances to put points on the board, but had to settle for five field goal tries. Jason Sanders made four of those kicks, but the Jets needed touchdowns that never came. They will host the Bills next Sunday and the 2-7 team figures to hear a lot more chatter about Aaron Glenn's job security in the wake of their fourth straight loss. Five of their first six losses were one-score games, but getting outscored 21-0 in the second half on Sunday doesn't make much of a case for Glenn having the team on the right path.

stories.title: Lions grind past Dolphins 19-9 as Jahmyr Gibbs scores and Jake Bates makes 4 field goals
stories.summary: — Jahmyr Gibbs had a rushing touchdown, Jared Goff threw for 170 yards and the Detroit Lions beat the Miami Dolphins 19-9 on Sunday for their fourth straight victory.
stories.detailText: MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- — Jahmyr Gibbs had a rushing touchdown, Jared Goff threw for 170 yards and the Detroit Lions beat the Miami Dolphins 19-9 on Sunday for their fourth straight victory. Jake Bates made four field goals on a day that was a bit underwhelming for Goff and the Lions' top-ranked offense, which entered averaging 29 points and 395.4 yards per game but finished with 271 yards. Goff completed 17 of 25 passes while being sacked three times as Miami's defense pressured him throughout. Goff was intercepted by rookie cornerback Chris Johnson on a tipped pass in the first quarter — just the second pick he has thrown this season. Gibbs averaged just 3.7 yards per carry, finishing with 74 yards on 20 attempts and an 8-yard rushing score that put the Lions ahead 16-6 entering the fourth. All-Pro Amon-Ra St. Brown had 86 yards receiving for the Lions, who are trying to keep pace in a tough NFC North. Lions players arrived at Hard Rock Stadium wearing No. 46 jerseys to honor All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell , who was placed on injured reserve this week after he was hospitalized with a scary neck injury suffered during last Sunday's win over Minnesota. Campbell's jersey was hanging in his locker at the stadium, and some fans raised signs that read “Campbell Strong.” The Lions never trailed but could not pull away from the rebuilding Dolphins, who had been in four consecutive one-score games entering Sunday. Bates made kicks of 28, 33, 40 and 43 yards. His 43-yarder gave Detroit a 10-point lead with 4:28 remaining. The Lions led 9-6 with four minutes left in the third when Goff connected with Jameson Williams for a 31-yard pickup — Detroit’s longest play of the game — that set up Gibbs' touchdown run on fourth down, his 11th scrimmage TD this season. Then the Dolphins took a page out Dan Campbell's book of aggressive play-calling, executing a fake punt that gave Miami the ball at Detroit's 18, setting up a 34-yard field goal by Zane Gonzalez . Malik Willis completed 13 of 25 passes for 128 yards and an interception while facing constant pressure from Detroit's front. The Dolphins went 0 for 3 in the red zone and failed to top 100 yards rushing for the second straight game. And despite staying within striking distance, the Dolphins had far too many self-inflicted wounds — including 11 penalties, a missed field goal and a kickoff that fell short of the landing zone. Both teams run successful fake punts Dolphins punter Bradley Pinion connected with Kaytron Allen for a 46-yard completion on Miami's fourth-quarter fake punt. In the second quarter, Jack Fox lined up to punt before tossing an 11-yard pass to Tay Martin , which gave Detroit the ball at the 41. The Dolphins' defense held, though, sacking Goff on third down to force a real punt. Injuries Dolphins: TE Will Kacmarek (quad) was injured after a low hit in the third quarter. He remained down for a couple of minutes before walking to the sideline unassisted. Up next Lions: Travel to Germany, where they will face New England in Munich next Sunday. Dolphins: At Indianapolis next Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: Chiefs-Jets: 4 instant takeaways from the bounce-back victory
stories.summary: Kansas City got back on track with a win that turned to dominant fashion against New York.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images In Week 9, the Kansas City Chiefs defeated the New York Jets 35-12 to move to 6-2. Here are 4 instant takeaways from the game : 1. Kenneth Walker reinforces his importance to team success After the Chiefs’ first two losses of the season, both games featured far less of running back Kenneth Walker than the initial five-game start, the offense got back on track by featuring its top playmaker. The lead back finished with 143 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns over 22 touches. Most of his production came through the air: for his first score, he leaked into the opposite flat in the red zone and outflanked his coverage responsibility to finish off a seven-yard touchdown pass. On the second, he caught a screen pass and, with great blocks from right guard Trey Smith and left guard Kingsley Suamataia, ran down the right sideline into the end zone from 25 yards away. Still, his carries showcased his individual talent the most. As he chipped away at 102 rushing yards, he was constantly staying up through contact or making defenders grasp at air with his elusiveness. The threat of his gashes opened things up against the Denver Broncos last week, and that continued alongside his own impactful gains against New York. It certainly made a difference to have Suamataia back on the field, but the game plan to lean on Walker was smart and effective. He is the engine of an in-rhythm offense in Kansas City. 2. The Chiefs’ pass rush is heating up Whatever criticism the Chiefs’ pass rush faced heading into this game, it was silenced. Defensive tackle Chris Jones needs to be more impactful? How about two big-time sacks all by himself? He beat a guard quickly on one play, then flew around the right edge before plowing quarterback Geno Smith into the grass in the fourth quarter. Defensive end George Karlaftis needs to do more than bat balls down? How about finishing with two sacks, another tackle for loss, and a separate quarterback hit? Oh yeah, and he also batted a pass down. He is now the team leader in both passes defended (9) and sacks(4). Other players need to win around Jones and Karlaftis? Defensive end Ashton Gillotte was relentless on his way to a sack that cost the offense 14 yards. Kansas City had five sacks, and none of them came from a blitz. 3. Weak links in pass protection can’t be hidden Right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) left the game in the second half and didn’t return; Joshua Ezeudu replaced him. Before he went out, Moore was having a very hard time with Jets’ rookie edge rusher David Bailey — the No. 2 pick in this year’s draft. The phenom finished with two sacks, two forced fumbles, and an additional quarterback hit. The biggest hit he allowed left Mahomes with a hurt throwing elbow late in the first half. The two-time MVP walked to the sideline with his right arm hanging loose, but never missed a snap and didn’t let the injury noticeably hamper him more than the constant pressure itself did. The Jets registered eight quarterback hits and two sacks over 34 dropbacks by Mahomes, despite the offense having a rhythm for much of the game. It speaks to Kansas City’s lack of answers for an elite edge rusher like Bailey when those matchups come up in the future. 4. *cringes* It’s Justin Tucker time After the 51-yard miss in perfect football conditions at his home stadium — which followed a 56-yard miss negated by a penalty — the era of kicker Harrison Butker feels all but over. Get ready for Justin Tucker to kick for the team against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 10.

stories.title: CeeDee Lamb’s fumble vs. the Colts is the most chaotic play of the NFL season
stories.summary: You have to see this CeeDee Lamb fumble.
stories.detailText: The 2026 NFL campaign is just reaching the midway point of the regular season. But you might not find a wilder play than this fumble by Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts. With the visiting Cowboys facing a 3rd-and-12 in their own territory, while holding a 20-17 lead, Indianapolis brought the blitz against quarterback Dak Prescott. With several pass rushers in his face, Prescott got off a throw to Lamb along the right sideline. Because Prescott was unable to step into the throw, the pass was underthrown and Lamb had to break back to the football. Which he did, making a diving catch in front of rookie cornerback Kenneth Harris. And that is exactly when the chaos began. Harris slipped on his own break, and that allowed Lamb enough separation to make the diving catch. But Harris never touchdown Lamb down, who alertly got to his feet and raced upfield, picking up a block as he sliced into the red zone. That’s when he was tackled, lost the ball, and following a challenge from Colts head coach Shane Steichen, Indianapolis took over possession. You can see the entire sequence here: A LOT JUST HAPPENED DALvsIND on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/zG2BwXaqlh — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 The FOX Sports booth speculated that because he is a rookie, Harris believed in the moment that Lamb did not need to be touched down. After all, in the college game once a player goes to the ground with the football, they are down at that spot and the play is whistled dead. Instead, he gave Lamb a chance to pick up additional yardage, only for the Dallas WR to fumble the ball away after what was, for a brief moment, a brilliant play. And no one was happier for that fumble than Harris.

stories.title: Lions vs. Dolphins final score, immediate winners, losers, reactions
stories.summary: The Dolphins came up short as they tried to go toe-to-toe against the Detroit Lions and the NFL’s top offense.
stories.detailText: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 08: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions scrambles with the ball against the Miami Dolphins during the third quarter at Hard Rock Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins’ Week 9 schedule brought the NFL’s top-ranked offense to Hard Rock Stadium as the Detroit Lions came to South Florida. It was a tough matchup for a 1-6 team still trying to grow and develop with a roster full of rookies, but the Dolphins stood up and fought for all 60 minutes. Detroit put the game away late, but with the over/under set at 50.5 points for the day, a combined 28-point total reflects strong defensive play from both teams. Final Score Lions 19 – 9 Dolphins Immediate Reactions Snap Winners and Losers Winners Jeff Hafley, head coach The Dolphins defense showed up to play in this game. Hafley, the former Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator, clearly brought that experience to Miami and used it against the Lions today. The defense was ready to face the number one offense in the league and they did well for much of the game. They allowed one touchdown drive in the second half with a couple of big plays, but for the most part, Hafley’s defense was ready and executed well. Chop Robinson, edge Early in the season, frustration over Robinson’s lack of production was growing. Over the past few weeks, he put that behind him, and on Sunday, he was a force throughout the game. Josh Uche, edge Continuing with the defensive theme, Uche was disruptive throughout the game as well. Uche set the tone early, disrupting the run, setting the edge, deflecting the pass that led to a Chris Johnson interception. and getting a sack. He was a factor in the game, even if things fell off a little in the second half. Caleb Douglas, wide receiver Douglas dropped a late fourth-down attempt that would have given Miami a first down as they tried to come back, but aside from that, the rookie receiver had a day. He finished the game with six receptions for 70 yards. Losers Note: “Losers” is not a judgment on the talent or character of any individual. It is simply a categorization of the play in one game – no disrespect is intended or should be inferred Bradley Pinion, punter The Dolphins’ punter has struggled this year, especially in terms of consistency. Also serving as the kickoff specialist, Pinion was flagged on the opening kickoff for failing to get the ball into the landing zone. In the second quarter, he shanked a punt for just 25 yards. It was not a banner day for the Dolphins’ punter. Pinion did have a 46-yard pass to running back Kaytron Allen on a fake punt, which nearly pushed him off this list, but the season-long inconsistency keeps him here. Penalties So many flags were thrown against the Dolphins this week, especially against the offensive line. Counting declined penalties, Miami was flagged 12 times in the game. It feels more like a rookies trying too hard more than an issue of players not paying attention. Chris Bell, wide receiver Rookie receiver Chris Bell was just non-existent on Sunday. He was targeted one time and recorded no receptions. While Douglas continues to break out, Bell is struggling to produce. The potential is still there, and he will break out at some point, but right now, he is a complete afterthought for the offense. Other thoughts Dan Campbell comes home and brings others with him Lions head coach Dan Campbell’s first coaching job was with the Dolphins, starting as an intern, then as the tight ends coach, and ending as the team’s interim head coach after Joe Philbin was fired. Campbell showed flashes of what he would become as a head coach, but he was not yet ready to get the job full time. There was definitely temptation there. Campbell instead went to the New Orleans Saints as their tight ends and assistant head coach. Campbell moved to the Lions in 2021 and has worked therm through a rebuild into a team that should be a contender for a deep run in the NFC playoffs. After Campbell’s interim stint, Miami hired Adam Gase, then Brian Flores, then Mike McDaniel, and now Jeff Hafley. The Lions coaching staff also includes defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard, defensive line coach Kacy Rodgers, and outside linebackers coach David Carrao – all of whom were Dolphins players or coaches. Just a quick look at the Lions coaching staff including HC Dan Campbell, DC Kelvin Sheppard, d-line coach Kacy Rodgers, and OLB coach David Carrao. pic.twitter.com/T2jsF5VMoY — The Phinsider (@thephinsider) November 8, 2026 Malik Willis’s groin injury a factor Willis is clearly bothered by the groin injury that has been on the injury report for the last couple of weeks. He just doesn’t have the same mobility we have seen from him before. He tried a couple of times to run away from pressure, but he just didn’t have the speed to get going. He showed solid understanding of the situation and threw the ball away at times, but the lack of scrambling ability was very noticeable in the game. Teams continue to forget to be special Pinion’s struggles (and the fake punt) were mentioned above, but overall, the Dolphins’ special teams still aren’t special. They gave up a fake punt, Zane Gonzalez blasted the upright on a field goal attempt to end the half, and overall, it feels like Miami cannot trust their special teams this year.

stories.title: Lions' defense shuts down Malik Willis and the Dolphins in 19-9 win
stories.summary: It wasn't pretty, but the Lions got the job done in Miami.
stories.detailText: The Lions' defense was playing with heavy hearts today in Miami, knowing that their leader Jack Campbell is still in a Detroit hospital after suffering a spinal injury a week ago. But the Lions heeded the call from head coach Dan Campbell to play in a way that would honor Jack Campbell. On a day when Detroit's offense was not at its best, the defense stepped up, holding Malik Willis & Co. in check in a 19-9 win. Derrick Moore sacked Willis twice, Alim McNeil sacked him once, and Aidan Hutchinson forced the Dolphins to hold him multiple times as Willis was under pressure all day. Willis finished 13-for-25 for 128 yards, with no touchdowns and one interception, and he managed only seven rushing yards. Lions quarterback Jared Goff could manage only 170 yards on 17-for-25 passing, but that was enough on a day when the Lions' defense played so well. Both punters completed passes for first downs on fake punts, and they were two of the best passes of the game on a day when neither Willis nor Goff played well. The win improves the Lions' record to 6-2, and helps them keep pace in the very competitive NFC North. The Dolphins fall to 1-7 and keep pace in their quest for the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft.

KC Concepcion got loose in the secondary and caught a 64-yard touchdown to give the Browns a 13-9 lead over New Orleans in the fourth quarter. Concepcion had gone down late in the third quarter with an apparent leg injury. But he was able to come back into the game without missing much time, and was clearly OK while speeding down the field. stories.title: Broncos DB Devon Key awarded wild interception in the Panthers' end zone after Denver challenge
stories.summary: The play had to be reviewed to confirm that the ball bounced off the hand of Carolina TE Tommy Tremble before Key plucked it out of the air.
stories.detailText: In Sunday’s matchup between the Carolina Panthers and the Denver Broncos, a dropped touchdown pass turned into an unbelievable interception thanks to a well-timed challenge. Towards the end of the third quarter, Panthers quarterback Bryce Young threw a pass to tight end Tommy Tremble in the end zone. Though the ball did end up in the hands of Broncos defensive back Devon Key, it looked like it hit the ground first, leading officials to rule the play an incomplete pass. However, Denver used its challenge flag, leading to a review that proved successful for the Broncos. As Tremble went down while trying to make the catch, the ball rolled off his wrist before bouncing off his hand, with Key in just the right position to pluck it out of the air. It never actually hit the ground at all, leading officials to overturn the call and rule it a Denver pick. Perfect place at the perfect time! Devon Key with an improbable INT for the @Broncos ! DENvsCAR on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/AnjjfvlHFi — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 Because the play was ruled dead, Key did not get a chance to make a return, but the Broncos were given a touchback as a result of the call. Quarterback Bo Nix then led the team down the field on a 14-play, 80-yard touchdown drive to take a 19-15 lead, after Denver’s two-point conversion attempt was unsuccessful. The game stayed tight until the end: Though the Broncos scored another fourth-quarter touchdown shortly afterwards, the Panthers came back with Young finding Tetairoa McMillan in the end zone on the next drive. A three-and-out Denver drive gave Carolina a late chance for a go-ahead touchdown, but Nik Bonitto forced Young’s second turnover of the night with a sack and fumble recovery. The Broncos then rode out the final minute and change for a 26-21 win ; they are now 7-2 on the season.

stories.title: The Broncos’ fingertip interception was wild and shouldn’t have been allowed
stories.summary: This was a wild interception, and the Panthers might have been screwed.
stories.detailText: The Denver Broncos have one of the most fearsome defenses in the NFL, not just because they hit hard, but also because they have ballhawks in the secondary. Denver entered its Week 9 matchup with the Carolina Panthers tied for seventh in the league in interceptions, and they added another one at the end of the third quarter in one of the wildest plays of the season for multiple reasons. Carolina QB Bryce Young threw the ball into the end zone for tight end Tommy Tremble, but it was successfully defended by Denver linebacker Justin Strnad. Tremble made a second effort to catch the ball, and it never actually hit the ground, staying in the air just long enough for Broncos defensive back Devon Key to grab it with his fingertips. It sure seemed like Key picked up the ball off the turf in real time. The Panthers lined up for the next play, and snapped the ball, running it with Chuba Hubbard. THEN the refs whistled and said they saw Payton’s challenge flag before Carolina snapped the ball, and reviewed the interception by Denver. It turns out Key grabbed the ball before it hit the turf, resulting in an interception. Watch the play here: Perfect place at the perfect time! Devon Key with an improbable INT for the @Broncos ! DENvsCAR on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/AnjjfvlHFi — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 Here’s another angle of the pick that clearly shows Key grabbed the ball before it hit the ground. That’s the real question. The refs’ decision to honor the challenge changed the game, because Denver went down and scored a touchdown after the interception. The Broncos just always seem to have luck on their side in the regular season. This is a ridiculous pick by Key either way.

stories.title: Puka Nacua's 14th catch goes for TD, Rams lead 20-13

stories.title: Burrow powers Bengals past the Falcons in Madrid for their 4th straight win
stories.summary: — Joe Burrow threw for three touchdowns and rushed for another and the Cincinnati Bengals' offense kept rolling to defeat the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 in Madrid on Sunday for their fourth straight win.
stories.detailText: MADRID -- — Joe Burrow threw for three touchdowns and rushed for another and the Cincinnati Bengals ' offense kept rolling to defeat the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 in Madrid on Sunday for their fourth straight win. Ja’Marr Chase had eight receptions for 142 yards in a career-high first half for him. Tee Higgins added two touchdown catches at Real Madrid's Santiago Bernabeu Stadium. Chase finished with 10 catches for 155 yards and a touchdown. After his 47-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter, Chase celebrated with Higgins in bullfighting style, with Higgins mimicking a bull by putting his hands on his head and Chase playing the matador with an imaginary cape. “It was one of my best performances," Chase said. "I just was getting good looks all day, honestly. I can say that. Joe was just believing in me on those one-on-one matchups and every time he got the opportunity, he was just feeding me." Burrow appeared to celebrate his rushing touchdown by imitating a celebration by Brazil soccer great Neymar, who used to play for Barcelona, holding his hands beside his helmet and wiggling his fingers. “I wanted to come out and put on a show for everybody and show what the excitement of the NFL can be,” said Burrow, playing in his first international game. “And the NFL is really all about the stars and players making big-time plays. And so you saw Ja'Marr Chase , you saw me, you see Tee Higgins, you saw a lot of great players out there doing great things. And hopefully people took notice.” The Bengals (6-2) have scored 30 points or more in four straight games for the first time since 1997, tying a franchise record. It was the second consecutive defeat for the Falcons (3-6). Burrow, who completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards Sunday, had thrown five touchdown passes and rushed for another in overtime in the team’s 43-36 win over the Tennessee Titans last week. “Joe’s playing at an unbelievably high level right now,” Bengals coach Zac Taylor said. “It’s difficult to not put the ball in his hands, given how everybody’s playing around him as well. So we just gotta keep this momentum going.” The Bengals failed to convert on third down only once in the first half and didn’t punt until their first drive in the second half. The Bengals scored on every possession before halftime, with three touchdowns and a field goal in the final seconds of the half. Playing under the closed roof of the Bernabeu, Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr . played better than in the rain in a 16-0 loss to the Buccaneers in Tampa Bay last week, but threw a late interception to go along with his opening-drive touchdown to tight end Charlie Woerner . Penix was 20 of 31 for 162 yards with a touchdown and interception and added 50 yards rushing. “We beat ourselves in a lot of areas of the game, and it’s tough,” Penix said. “We got to clean those things up. There is nothing that the guys don’t know. We go into the locker room after the game and it is like, we know what happened up there. We knew that was not who we wanted to be, who we want to be this season.” Running back Bijan Robinson had 42 yards on three carries on the Falcons' first drive. He ended with 100 yards rushing and a touchdown on 19 carries and 47 yards receiving on six receptions. “We were not good enough, we have to do better,” Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said. “We just were not at our best. And if you’re not at your best versus a good team, you’re not going to win.” It was the second NFL regular-season game in Madrid after the Miami Dolphins beat the Washington Commanders 16-13 in overtime in last year’s inaugural game in the country. It was the seventh game in a record nine-game schedule outside the U.S. for the NFL this season. The remaining games will be played in Munich, Germany, and Mexico City. A crowd of 78,660 people was on hand on Sunday in the Spanish capital. Bengals fans appeared to outnumber Falcons supporters. The lights at the Bernabeu suddenly went out just as the Bengals were taking a snap inside the final two minutes, prompting the down to be replayed. Early in the game, some Bengals defensive players appeared to change into longer spikes after the first drive to adjust to the grass at the Bernabeu. It was the Bengals’ first win in an international game. They had tied Washington in 2016 and lost to the Los Angeles Rams in 2019, both times in London. Falcons edge rusher James Pearce Jr . returned from an eight-game suspension for violating the NFL’s personal conduct policy but had limited play. Pearce had a back issue in Friday’s practice and had been listed as questionable ahead of the game. Before kickoff, a moment of silence was held in tribute to the victims of the high-speed train crash that killed 69 people in central Spain on Oct. 28, including four Americans. Spain’s World Cup trophies for both the women’s and men’s soccer teams were displayed on the field, with national team players on hand as well. Former Real Madrid and Brazil soccer great Roberto Carlos sounded the train horn in the Falcons' traditional pregame celebration. The halftime show featured Colombian music star Manuel Turizo. Up next Bengals: host Steelers on “Sunday Night Football” on Nov. 15. Falcons: host Kansas City on Sunday. ------ Associated Press writer Teresa Medrano contributed to this report. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: Lions and Dolphins are trading successful fake punts in Week 9
stories.summary: Punters Jack Fox and Bradley Pinion each have a completion in Lions-Dolphins
stories.detailText: They are trading completions in South Beach between the visiting Detroit Lions and the Miami Dolphins. And that is not limited to quarterbacks Jared Goff and Malik Willis. Both teams have now pulled off successful fake punts in this game, with punters Jack Fox and Bradley Pinion getting in on the passing game fun. Detroit was first to call for a fake punt, early in the second quarter. With the Lions facing a 4th-and-7 on their own 19-yard line, Dan Campbell rolled the dice. But Fox delivered a strike, throwing a near-perfect hitch route to Tay Martin along the left side of the field: What a throw, @MrJackFox pic.twitter.com/n3m4I5phod — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 8, 2026 With this timing and anticipation, one almost wonders if Fox once played quarterback. He did, throwing 18 touchdowns as a quarterback at Ladue Horton Watkins high school in Ladue, Missouri. Thanks to Ian Rapoport for dusting off that statistic. Not to be outdone, the Dolphins dialed up a creative fake punt of their own in the second half. With Miami facing a 4th-and-3 near midfield early in the fourth quarter, Jeff Hafley rolled the dice himself, with Pinion finding a wide-open Kaytron Allen for the first down. Take note of this design, as Allen comes underneath the line and releases through the middle of the formation, making this an easy throw for the punter: Dolphins draw up a fake punt of their own! That's two fake punts this game. DETvsMIA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/caEvejdds1 — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 Only one of these fakes resulted in points, however. The Lions were forced to punt a few plays later after their fake, while the Dolphins turned their extended possession into a field goal. Update: According to Scott Hanson on RedZone , this is the first game in league history where both punters completed a pass.

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are in action after their bye. They’ll host the Las Vegas Raiders, who have been a sneaky-good offense this season. Kirk Cousins is playing at a high level in the year 2026. The Raiders are fifth in passing EPA. A big reason why is Brock Bowers, who is one of the best skill players in the NFL. He’s proven to be unguardable. The 49ers will have their hands full with Bowers. The Raiders are one-dimensional, though. Ashton Jeanty was soft-benched a week ago. Rookie Mike Washington took his place with 25 carries, but only had 83 yards. Las Vegas also stalls out in the red zone. They’re scoring a touchdown at a 53% clip. Settling for field goals against the Niners is a death knell. A defensive line with Nick Bosa and DeForest Buckner should make life miserable on the Raiders. On the other side of the ball, George Kittle should have a big afternoon. Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black should find plenty of running room, too. We’ll see how much the wide receivers are involved. This game will be won in the red zone. The 49ers are scoring over 86% of the time. The offense should take its frustrations out on the Raiders, having not had the ball much against Atlanta and making several mistakes when they did.

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Las Vegas Raiders starting cornerback Darien Porter is active to play at the San Francisco 49ers. Kickoff is at 1:25 p.m. PT. The 2025 third-round draft pick was listed as questionable on the injury report to play in Week 9. Porter injured his groin on the first defensive play of the Raiders’ 38-33 victory at the New York Jets on Sunday. He didn’t practice Wednesday, but did work on Thursday and Friday. Rookie draft picks Jermod McCoy and Zeke Masses rotated in Porter’s absence in Week 8. Meanwhile, veteran backup defensive tackle Thomas Booker is out with a foot injury. He didn’t practice Thursday or Friday. The absence of Booker won’t change the Raiders’ rotation at defensive tackle much against San Francisco. There were no other Las Vegas players on the injury report.
